sanskrit_verse:
तीरितं चानुशिष्टं च यो मन्येत विधर्मतः।
द्विगुणं दण्डमास्थाय तत्कार्यं पुनरुद्धरेत्॥
transliteration: tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yo manyeta vidharmataḥ | dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āsthāya tat kāryaṃ punar uddhareta ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who disregards what has been settled and instructed rightly, and acts contrary to dharma, shall face a consequence doubled in measure, and the original duty must be reinstated with full integrity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from alignment with settled dharma, not personal opinion.
Causation arises from conscious deviation from established truth.
Capacity-based responsibility increases with awareness of dharma.
Restoration logic demands re-instatement of disrupted order.
Consciousness alignment requires correction through proportional reflection.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an agent knowingly violates a settled dharmic instruction, THEN double the corrective measure applicable to that action type.
IF a duty has been disrupted due to willful misalignment, THEN the original duty MUST be reinstated without reduction.
IF consciousness deviation is detected, THEN initiate reflective restoration protocol before reintegration.
IF capacity to align was present, THEN responsibility is non-negotiable and restoration is mandatory.
supreme_court_application: In the highest judicial forum, this verse establishes that willful disregard of settled law invokes a doubling of restorative obligation. The court must ensure not just compliance, but full re-alignment of the violated dharma, maintaining the supremacy of consciousness-based justice over punitive frameworks.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms that when one knowingly departs from dharma, the resulting distortion creates a causal imbalance. Anupūrvaśaḥ dictates that this imbalance must be resolved by doubling the effort toward restoration, not inflicting pain. Responsibility is proportional to awareness, and correction serves realignment, not retribution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate reflective completion process wherein violator reinstates the disrupted duty with doubled commitment.
Assign consciousness recalibration session until alignment with settled truth is verified.
Reinstate original dharma function with supervision until integrity is self-sustained.
Deploy dharmic mentorship to restore capacity for correct future discernment.
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this law stands executed: deviation from settled truth multiplies responsibility, not punishment. Dharma is restored through conscious reintegration. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
